status: Not selected as implemented; both complex-product prototypes remain isolated.
decision: The common-scale three-product idea has established wide-input gains, but this global dispatch insertion is not justified under the requested retention priorities. It adds no exactness or completeness capability, retains measurable bypass/reused-control costs, increases peak demand in 33 groups, and grows the benchmark binaries. Do not transfer v2 into the live crates.
evidence: Fresh paired CPU campaign: 55 of 60 candidate-reaching groups have per-group intervals below parity, none above, five overlapping. Across all 192 groups: 66 below, 17 above, 109 overlapping. All 17 above-parity intervals are bypass/reused controls. Intervals are not multiplicity-adjusted and do not establish universal effects. Memory improvements relative to v1 and remaining baseline costs are both retained in the evidence.
limits: V2 changes the crossover, dispatch and temporary lifetime together; this is not a factorial attribution experiment. No new full crate/debug/state-history/concurrency/internal-unreduced-storage/quotient timing/representative application-size qualification is claimed. No theorem that every three-product implementation is unsuitable follows.
next: Resume the remaining original source audit, starting with Arb dot-product and error-bound support. The wide common-scale idea may be revisited for a measured application that predominantly reaches it, but do not keep iterating generic dispatch variants without new workload evidence. All original references and full inventory reconciliation remain in scope.
